newsitem.title: USA: CME May lumber ends limit up on stronger cash.
newsitem.headline: CME May lumber ends limit up on stronger cash.

text.p: May CME lumber futures ended up their $10.00 limit as reports of higher cash trade sparked shortcovering, traders said.
May ended limit up at $391.60 per tbf, with July up $8.60 at $387.40. Other months settled $4.10 higher to $2.00 lower with only distant January off.
Futures ran up following reports of increased cash trade with buy stops touched off above Monday's highs. Cash sources reported that spruce was trading in the $395 to $400 area.
That compares to Friday's quote of $390.

Demand for wood, especially wider widths, at mills increased Tuesday morning and this prompted commercial buying in futures. The large discount of futures to cash had been supporting futures early, traders added.
"There's been a resumption of the trade in the cash," said Curt Cunningham, President Pacific Futures Trading.
Refco was a notable buyer of May and July on the advance. ING was an early seller, pit sources added.
